deck_zh: 有另一家店，是否就有另一条路？从 Amazon 的价格、Prime 与物流争议，看有价值的整合怎样接受追问。
deck_en: Another storefront is not necessarily another usable route. Amazon's pricing and fulfilment dispute asks how valuable integration can remain open to challenge.
search_labels: Amazon 亚马逊 Marketplace Prime FBA Buy Box Featured Offer 平台 物流 反折价 欧盟 承诺决定 FTC antitrust fulfilment fulfillment anti-discounting
body_zh: 在 Amazon 的反垄断案卷里，一个反复出现的争点，并不是卖家有没有权另开一家店。争的是：货可以放到别处，顾客、价格和配送能不能一起过去。一个账号能注册成功，离一门生意能在另一处活下来，还不是同一件事。
先看买家面前的一处小地方。同一件商品可能有几位卖家提供报价，而醒目的购买位置只突出其中一个。案卷沿用 Buy Box 这个名称，购买界面也会使用 Featured Offer 的说法。对买家，这是少找几步的便利；对卖家，哪一份报价被放在眼前，就成为需要认真对待的条件。[1][4]
再往后，是 Prime 的配送承诺，以及 FBA——卖家把仓储、打包、发货等工作交给 Amazon 的履约服务。三者相关，却不是同一个东西：一个是报价展示，一个是会员服务及相应资格，一个是处理订单的办法。把它们混成一个按钮，问题便看不清了。[1][3]
美国联邦贸易委员会与州方在2023年起诉 Amazon，后来修订诉状。他们指控，一组相互加强的做法限制了竞争，其中包括对站外低价的反应，以及把 Prime 资格与 FBA 紧密连接。Amazon 否认这些指控，认为原告把有利于顾客和卖家的竞争写反了。[1][3]
本文所读案件截至2026年11月1日，不能写成实体责任已经判定。法院2024年允许核心联邦主张继续，并不意味着它已经确认原告讲述的事实。2026年10月30日的程序令仍在安排可能终结案件的动议与专家证据动议的文件处理。程序走到了哪里，文章就只能说到哪里。[2][6]
## 便利从哪里来
一个小商家自己找顾客、收款、储货、处理退货，需要做许多不属于制作商品本身的事。把这些工作交给一个熟悉的系统，可能省下时间，也可能得到原来够不到的订单。不能因为系统后来握有很大影响，就把人们最初为什么愿意进来写成谜。
Amazon 的答辩值得照它最强的样子读。公司说，FBA 是可选服务，它通过多年物流投入提供仓储、包装、配送与退货处理；卖家也可以使用别的履约方式，达到要求时还可通过其他物流服务取得 Prime 标识。公司强调，消费者信任快速、可靠的配送，这种标准本身有价值。[3]
在价格问题上，Amazon 的解释是，不应突出推荐对顾客不划算的报价。零售商比较别处的价格，再决定哪些商品值得推广，公司认为这属于竞争，而不是破坏竞争。若要求它忽略较低报价，反而可能使消费者付得更多。[3]
这个理由不能只被当成一层需要揭穿的包装。便利与信任需要投入，低价也确实是顾客在乎的东西。如果一种整改使配送更不可靠、比较更困难，它就有必须说明的代价。但这个理由仍未回答全部问题：被改善的体验，与被限制的替代，是不是只能这样捆在一起？
也正因此，营业额有多大，并不能独自完成判断。一个平台很大，可能是因为它做成了很多事；也可能在某些具体规则里，使别的办法越来越难长出来。这两种说明能否同时成立，不能只凭规模，也不能只凭受欢迎。要往下读条款怎样发生作用。
## 另一家店，怎样才成为另一条路
FTC 的反折价主张，指向一个容易被一句“卖家自己定价”遮住的地方。原告称，卖家若在其他网站以更低价格销售，可能受到 Amazon 在展示或推荐上的不利处理。这是原告提出的机制，不是本文已经独立量出的普遍效果。[1]
按这一主张，一次降价的后果不只留在降价的那家店。卖家本来想在另一个渠道少付一些费用、卖得便宜一点，却还得考虑在原平台失去展示会怎样。这样，站外开店的自由仍然存在，站外怎样卖却受到另一处入口的影响。这个因果链要经证据检验；它至少说清了应该查哪几步。
Amazon 看见的是另一面：既然外面同一件商品更便宜，为什么这里还要把较贵报价放在最显眼的位置？这道反问有力量。需要判的不是顾客该不该看见低价，而是具体执行方式在什么市场条件下，究竟促进了降价，还是使卖家不敢在别处降价。两种作用不能由同一句口号分出胜负。[2][3]
Prime 与物流的争议，把这件事再推深一点。起诉状称，Prime 资格对许多卖家的销售很重要，取得资格又通常被系在 FBA 上。于是，一个想在多个渠道卖货的人，可能需要分开库存，或者承担跨渠道履约的额外成本。原告认为，这会妨碍卖家选择一个能同时服务多处的独立物流体系。[1]
这里应当把争议原样留着。Amazon 说服务是可选的，其他路径也存在；FTC 说存在路径，不代表那条路在它描述的时期、对相关卖家有可比的实际条件。不能替所有卖家虚构一笔损失，也不能用某个卖家成功采用其他办法，便替每种处境结案。
一家店是否是真正可用的替代，需要逐项看：能接触到哪些买家，库存能否共用，费用如何形成，服务标准怎样验证，转换要花多久。其中有些成本是另建网络本来就有的，有些可能来自原有规则；要区分，不能看见成本就宣布它是排挤，也不能看见合同就停止调查。
法院在2024年的裁定中，专门说明了一个程序问题：此阶段要按有利于原告的方式阅读充分提出的事实主张，不能仅凭诉状就结清促进竞争的利益与排除竞争的效果。Amazon 的质量与低价理由没有因此被证明错误；FTC 的理论也没有因此被证明正确。留下审理的空间，本身正是区别。[2]
## 不只是叫人离开
如果问题确实出在规则里，答案也未必只是劝卖家离开，或者要求整个系统被拆掉。可以先问得更具体：为了确保准时送达，必须由谁送？为了筛选好报价，必须排除哪些条件？一项标准有理由存在，是否意味着制定者的每一种执行方式都有理由？
欧洲的另一段记录，提供了可供比较的安排，而不是美国案的判决。2022年12月，欧盟委员会使 Amazon 提出的承诺具有法律约束力，涉及非公开卖家数据的零售使用、Buy Box 报价选择，以及 Prime 的资格和承运商选择。它还包括监督与投诉方面的安排。[4]
委员会的官方说明把边界写得很清楚：这种承诺决定不作违反欧盟竞争规则的认定，却使企业必须遵守承诺。Amazon 同时表示相信自己的模式与做法符合欧洲法律。因此，不能把它讲成公司承认了美国诉状，也不能把承诺本身当作成效已经实现的报告。[4][5]
这一比较有用的地方，在于问题被分开了。要保留配送标准，可以讨论怎样让别的承运商按可检查的标准参与；要避免数据被竞争中的自营业务使用，可以问谁能接触什么；要让另一份报价被看见，可以检查展示，而不只在网页深处再添一个入口。具体做法是否足够，仍要追踪执行。
对负责检查的人，也要继续问。谁能提交投诉，什么材料拿得到，多久有答复，出现分歧谁重看？由一个平台自己解释所有规则，并不是唯一可能；把解释移交外部，也不是从此不会出错。改变一项规则有代价，维持它同样有代价，两边都应当说清。
这里还藏着一个比“退出”更宽的问题。有些卖家愿意留下，他们需要的不是被教育到别处去，而是有地方追问自己必须遵守的条件。提出异议不等于否认平台的贡献，继续使用服务也不等于认可每项安排。一个人可以真心需要这里，同时要求这里有所改变。
这篇文章不替尚未审结的案件预写结论，也不把欧洲承诺复制成所有市场的答案。它只是顺着报价、配送与顾客入口，把一句熟悉的话拆开：可以去别处卖，说明还有一个去处；怎样使那个去处长成可用的路，以及留下的人怎样仍能说话，还要另外作答。
body_en: The dispute in Amazon's antitrust case is not simply whether a seller can open another store. It is about what can travel with the seller: access to customers, room to price differently and a workable way to fulfil orders. Registering an account elsewhere and sustaining a business there are different achievements.

Begin with a small part of the product page. Several sellers may offer the same item, but a prominent purchase position highlights one offer. The filings use the familiar name Buy Box; shoppers may also encounter Featured Offer. For a customer it shortens the search. For a seller, the route by which an offer reaches that position can matter a great deal.[1][4]

Behind the offer sit Prime's service promise and eligibility requirements, and Fulfillment by Amazon, or FBA: services through which Amazon handles work such as storage, packing and delivery. Display, membership and fulfilment interact, but they are not the same thing. Combining them into one vague idea of a platform conceals the decisions we need to examine.[1][3]

The FTC and state plaintiffs sued Amazon in 2023 and subsequently amended their complaint. Their case alleges an interlocking course of conduct, including responses to lower prices off Amazon and conditions connecting Prime eligibility to FBA. Amazon rejects the account and argues that the plaintiffs have mistaken competition benefiting shoppers and sellers for harm.[1][3]

As of this essay's cutoff, 1 November 2026, the allegations discussed here must not be presented as an adjudication of liability. The 2024 decision allowing the core federal claims to proceed was an early-stage ruling. An order dated 30 October 2026 still addressed filings for dispositive and expert-evidence motions. That procedural position belongs in the story, not in an easily forgotten disclaimer.[2][6]
## The value of putting things together

A small business must do more than make an attractive product. It has to find customers, collect payment, keep stock and deal with returns. A system that takes on part of this work can make a market reachable that was previously out of range. The reasons for joining do not become unreal when the system's rules are challenged.

Amazon's own response deserves to be read at its strongest. The company describes FBA as optional and as the result of substantial investment in logistics. It says sellers can choose other fulfilment methods, and that other logistics services can support the Prime badge when they meet the required delivery standards. A reliable promise to the customer, on this account, needs a reliable means of keeping it.[3]

Its pricing argument is equally recognizable. A retailer should not have to promote an offer that is a poor deal for the shopper. Amazon says comparing prices and declining to highlight uncompetitive offers protects customer trust. Preventing those practices, it argues, could leave shoppers paying more rather than less.[3]

Those explanations should not be treated merely as camouflage. Reliability has to be built, and price matters. A remedy that damages delivery or makes comparison harder has costs it must explain. But a real benefit does not yet establish that every condition attached to obtaining it is necessary. The question is whether the benefit and the particular restriction must travel together.

Size alone cannot answer. A large network may have grown by doing useful work; some of its rules may also make alternatives harder to establish. Both propositions require attention. Popularity does not settle every use of a position, and concentration does not by itself tell us which use is wrong.
## When another store is not another route

The FTC's anti-discounting claim concerns what happens outside Amazon. The plaintiffs allege that a seller offering a lower price on another website can face adverse consequences for visibility or promotion on Amazon. That is an alleged mechanism, not a universal effect independently measured by this essay.[1]

If the account is established, a discount's consequences do not remain in the place offering it. A seller considering lower fees and a lower price elsewhere must also consider what happens to access on the original platform. Freedom to open a second storefront can coexist with constraints reaching into how that storefront competes. The causal chain needs evidence; spelling it out identifies what the evidence would have to show.

Amazon asks a powerful question from the other direction: if the same item costs less elsewhere, why should this store feature the more expensive offer? The disagreement is not resolved by deciding that low prices are good. It turns on whether the particular practice, in the relevant market conditions, encourages lower prices or deters sellers from offering them outside. Both accounts cannot be settled by repeating the word competition.[2][3]

The fulfilment allegations add another layer. The complaint says Prime eligibility is important to many sellers and is generally conditioned on FBA. It argues that a seller seeking to operate across channels can then face inventory splitting or additional fulfilment costs, making a single independent network serving several outlets harder to use. These are the plaintiffs' claims about the challenged arrangements, not a description of every present-day seller's options.[1]

The disagreement must remain visible. Amazon says the services are optional and alternatives can work. The FTC alleges that an alternative's existence does not establish comparably usable conditions for the sellers and period it describes. One seller's successful alternative cannot answer for everyone, just as an alleged mechanism cannot supply an invented loss for a particular business.

A usable route has several parts: customers who can be reached, inventory that can be deployed, fees that can be understood, standards that can be verified and a transition that can be financed. Some costs arise from building another network. Others may arise from rules imposed by an existing one. Investigating that distinction is different from declaring every switching cost exclusionary.

The court's 2024 order helps preserve the distinction. On a motion to dismiss, sufficiently pleaded facts are read in the plaintiffs' favour; weighing asserted competitive benefits against alleged exclusionary effects is not resolved on the pleadings. The order does not establish that Amazon's quality and price explanations are false. Nor does it establish the FTC's causal account. It leaves matters for the evidentiary process.[2]

There is an editorial temptation to remove this uncertainty so the story can move faster. Doing so would remove part of the subject. Who has alleged, who has answered and who has decided are different positions. An essay about accountable decisions should not quietly take the last position for itself.
## The people who stay can ask too

If a problem lies in the rules, telling individual sellers to leave may not address it. Nor does identifying a problem automatically select a breakup. We can ask more specific questions first. What delivery performance is required? Who must perform it? Which criteria distinguish a good offer, and which criteria tie that offer to another service? A justified standard does not justify every method of administering it.

A separate European proceeding offers arrangements to compare, not a verdict in the American case. In December 2022, the European Commission made Amazon commitments legally binding concerning non-public seller data, Buy Box selection and Prime eligibility and carrier choice. The package also addressed monitoring and complaints.[4]

The Commission's official explanation explicitly distinguishes an Article 9 commitment decision from a finding that EU competition law was infringed. Amazon maintained that its model and practices complied with European law. Neither the decision nor the company's agreement to commitments is an admission of the American allegations. Nor is the announcement proof that every promised improvement subsequently reached sellers.[4][5]

The comparison is useful because it separates tasks. Delivery standards can be retained while asking how independent carriers qualify against verifiable conditions. Data use can be limited by specifying who may use which information. A competing offer can be made more visible rather than merely placed behind another link. Whether these measures work remains an implementation question, not something their announcement settles.

Review needs a route of its own. Who can complain? What information can they obtain? How long does an answer take, and who can revisit it? Having the platform explain every disputed rule is not the only possible design. Moving review outside the platform is not a guarantee of infallibility either. An intervention must explain its costs, as must a decision to leave an arrangement unchanged.

This opens a question larger than exit. Some sellers want to remain. What they need is not advice to become less dependent by sheer determination, but an effective way to question conditions they must meet. Challenging a rule does not deny the value of the service; using the service does not endorse every rule. Dependence can make a voice more necessary, not less legitimate.

The essay does not decide the pending case or turn European commitments into a ready-made solution for every market. It follows the connections between an offer, a delivery promise and access to customers. You can sell somewhere else identifies a possible destination. Whether that destination can become a usable route—and how those who stay can still be heard—requires a further answer.
